text:
alejandro: FYI I hit a blocking TypeScript error in the edge sample when consumers use NodeNext tsconfig. The stack points at our overloads in index.d.ts — unknown vs string.

alejandro: paste: TS2345: Argument of type 'unknown' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'. at createClient<T = any>(opts: CreateOptions<T>): Client

sasha: ugh. we've seen this pattern: different generic defaults across overloads + consumers using nodeNext cause inference to pick a bad signature. Edge bundlers make it worse because runtime and types can resolve different package entries.

taylor: Repro I used: create a fresh project, tsconfig with module: "NodeNext" and moduleResolution: "NodeNext", install @redwood/sdk, run `tsc --noEmit`. Fails. Switching to moduleResolution: "bundler" or module: "ES2022" makes it go away.

sasha: short-term sample patch: set skipLibCheck: true in sample tsconfig and call it out in README. That reduces noise for folks onboarding.

alejandro: also noticed the ESM browser build dropped our auth retry side-effect import, so on token refresh the sample sometimes 401s. CJS path keeps it.

taylor: that's the rollup/tree-shake parity issue. Workaround in sample: explicitly import '@redwood/sdk/compat/retries' in the entry so it isn't removed. We'll need a proper fix for prod bundles.

ci-bot: Created issue #950 in repo 'redwood-js' (https://git.redwood.com/issue/950) - labels: sdk, types, edge - assigned to @sasha

sasha: Proposed long-term actions: 1) Publish an "edge-friendly" types entry that points to flattened d.ts without overlapping overloads. 2) Add a non-overloaded factory export (eg createClientEdge<T = unknown>) to avoid inference ambiguity. 3) Add CI matrix that compiles the sample under NodeNext, Bundler, and typical edge toolchains. 4) Ensure bundler config keeps side-effect imports for compat shims.

taylor: I'll open a small PR to update the sample tsconfig + README with the NodeNext notes and the explicit import workaround.

alejandro: thanks. can we also add a short note in the SDK changelog explaining why unknown is preferred over any for safety? People keep overriding to any and then hitting runtime surprises.

sasha: good call. i'll add that to the issue checklist.

taylor: ping me on the PR for a quick review.

alejandro: landing this will save a lot of confused first-time contributors. :+1:
